Subject: Orbit Commerce — trial ops playbook & next tests

Thanks again for taking the time today, Alicia — good conversation and clear priorities. This thread is a short recap plus proposed next steps and owners so we have a single source of truth for the trial.

Call recap (high level):
- Goal: validate production cost & latency profile for inference across peak ecomm traffic (search + chat flows).
- Scope: 2 weeks of controlled load testing in your staging, comparing Redwood private-hosted runtime vs AWS Bedrock + Vertex API baseline you requested.
- Key constraints: data residency in us-east-1, S3-based artifacts for model inputs, PI/PII scrubbed prior to upload.

Proposed next tests (minimum viable):
1) Latency profile (p50/p95/p99) at target concurrency: 50 RPS sustained, 200 RPS burst.
2) Throughput and cost: tokens/1M and end-to-end $/1M tokens measured across identical prompt sets.
3) KV/prefix cache effectiveness for repeat traffic patterns (shopping history autofill).
4) Model consistency/regression: sampling stability & hallucination checks on a 250-case prompt suite.
5) Failure & fallback: simulated region outage to validate model routing/fallback behavior.

Success criteria (draft):
- p95 latency <= 250ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens) and p99 <= 450ms under target concurrency.
- Cost per 1M tokens at least 20% lower than the hyperscaler baseline or demonstrably better tail latency for a comparable cost.
- Cache hit rate >= 60% for repeated prefix patterns.
- No functional regressions on the 250-case prompt suite (pass/fail threshold 95% agreement vs baseline).

Owners & immediate asks:
- Ben Carter (AE): coordinate procurement paperwork, schedule access to staging, track timeline.
- Marissa Cole (Sales Eng): deliver test harness + config, run first-pass performance runs, build the result dashboard.
- Marcus Lin (Solutions Architect): standardize model variants and runtime config (quantization, KV settings), provide infra runbook.

Attachments & links: trial-playbook-v1.xlsx (detailed test matrix) attached; HubSpot deal link and Drive folder here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-trial-plan

Proposed timeline:
- 48 hours: Redwood provides sandbox credentials and a first-draft test harness (Marissa).
- Day 3–7: Baseline runs (hyperscaler + Redwood mirror).
- Day 8–11: Focused optimization (cache tuning, batching).
- Day 12–14: Final runs, QA, results deck.

Next step for you: can you confirm staging window availability for Feb 22–Mar 7 and who will own procurement/internal sign-off (PO or DS)?

Cheers,
Ben Carter

Appreciate the quick reply, Alicia — answered inline below and added a bit more detail on the comparison matrix you'll get.

> Data residency: we need all inference and logs to stay in us-east-1. Can Redwood guarantee that for the Private deployment sandbox?
Yes — for Private (VPC) and our dedicated-hosted sandbox we can pin everything to us-east-1. Logs can be routed to your KMS-protected bucket in the same region. Marcus (cc) will share the runbook for the VPC/network requirements.

> S3 connector: we have an S3 bucket with test artifacts and a few streaming inputs. Do you have an S3 ingestion connector or do we push objects?
We support both patterns. For the trial we'll provision a read-only IAM role so Redwood can pull artifacts directly. If you prefer push, we can accept signed URLs as well. Marissa — I'll let you coordinate the specifics.

> Concurrency: validate tail latency up to 400 RPS briefly.
We can absolutely include a brief burst to 400 RPS during baseline runs. If sustained 400 RPS required we may need to enable a small dedicated burst pool — we'll call that out in the run results.

> Comparative metrics: simple matrix p50/p95/p99 + $/1M tokens across Redwood vs Bedrock/Vertex/Azure OpenAI.
We'll deliver a one-page matrix (redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.pdf attached) after baseline runs. Important note: hyperscalers expose different pricing models (per-request vs token metering differences). We'll normalize to effective $/1M tokens and call out any assumptions.

I also want to explicitly call out Redwood differentiators we'll test for you:
- KV/prefix caching to reduce repeated token cost for session-based flows
- Continuous batching and dynamic kernel selection for long and short prompts
- Built-in model variant pinning so you can roll forward/back during tests without changing API calls
- Automatic multi-region fallback behavior for graceful degradation (we can simulate this)

Action items I will do by EOD tomorrow:
- Send the credentials/access instructions and test harness (Marissa will own the runs).
- Share procurement contact and a one-pager on standard MSA timelines.

Can you confirm Feb 24–27 as the preferred run window? If so we'll lock engineers on our side and circulate an updated schedule.

Thanks,
